text:
raj: quick sync - acme wants a private/vpc poc next week. they require sso (saml) traffic never traverse public internet, dual-stack where possible, and a short justification for privateLink vs peering. can netops/security weigh in? cc @leah :wave:

leah: tl;dr: privatelink isolates endpoints and gives tighter egress control and simpler firewall rules. vpc peering avoids connector fees but requires cross-account routing, extra route table entries, and exposes larger attack surface. if they demand private-only saml assertions, privatelink + a local saml bridge or a private deployment looks safest.

mike: ipv6 note - our GA privatelink connector is ipv4-only. we have an experimental dual-stack approach but it needs customer-side nat64/translation. if they need native ipv6 for data plane, thats a blocker until we ship dual-stack GA. for control-plane callbacks (saml) we can tunnel over privatelink in ipv4.

sam: security checklist items: 1) confirm "no internet transit" for saml assertions. 2) confirm they accept our public certs if TLS inspect is on. 3) if they require control-plane on-prem-only, escalate to sales/legal for private deployment terms. mark this HIGH risk for hosted control-plane + private-only saml.

raj: customer also asked about pricing - any connector or per-hour fees for privatelink?

leah: short answer: hosted privatelink connector has a monthly connector surcharge + per-gb egress. private deployment is a separate license (platform fee + support). i'll paste the pricing line after the call.

mike: minimal firewall snippet for customer to pre-provision:
```
# allow outbound https from customer app/subnet to our privatelink endpoint vpc ranges
TCP 443 -> 34.200.128.0/22  # control-plane callbacks (example CIDR)
TCP 443 -> 52.203.32.0/22   # model-serving egress (if using hosted serving)
# Optional: ICMP echo for health checks to 34.200.128.0/22
# If they require static egress IPs for callbacks: allow TCP 443 from our shared EIP pool (we will share list)
```

sam: note - if their perimeter does TLS SNI inspection, they must either allow SNI passthrough for our endpoints or install our cert PEM to avoid handshake failures with saml responses. also document KMS/key expectations if they require cert pinning.

mike: quick poc network checklist we can send to customer: 1) vpc (/20 recommended) or existing vpc with spare subnets 2) reserve private subnets for connector (no nat/gw required) 3) pre-authorize outbound https to our control-plane cidrs (we'll share) 4) if dual-stack required: provision nat64 or translation and validate with our test endpoints 5) if saml-private: spin up a tiny saml-bridge vm in their vpc that proxies assertions over privatelink to our control plane

raj: can ops/netops/security join a 3pm PT sync today? want to produce a short justification memo + firewall checklist to hand to buyer after the call.

leah: 3pm works for me. @mike @sam?

mike: yes, i'll bring connector cidrs and sample routing table snippets.

sam: yes, i'll bring redlined answers for the security questionnaire and list of acceptable crypto controls.

security-bot: FYI - customer ticked "no shared ip addresses with other customers". privatelink gives endpoint isolation but not necessarily dedicated hardware. if they need physical isolation, open a ticket for dedicated-hosting evaluation. :lock:

raj: thanks all. i'll schedule and share the pre-provision checklist after the call. :thumbsup:
